passages.text: Now the Philistines brought all their forces together at Aphek, while Israel camped by the spring in Jezreel.
passages.sermon: The Philistines gathered all their armies at Aphek.\r\nIsrael set up camp by the spring in Jezreel.
passages.original: וַיִּקְבְּצ֧וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֛ים אֶת־ כָּל־ מַחֲנֵיהֶ֖ם אֲפֵ֑קָה וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל חֹנִ֔ים בַּעַ֖יִן אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּיִזְרְעֶֽאל׃

passages.text: As the Philistine leaders marched out their units of hundreds and thousands, David and his men marched behind them with Achish.
passages.sermon:
The Philistine leaders marched out their troops.
They organized their troops in groups of hundreds and thousands.
David was with Achish.
David’s men were with him.
David and his men marched at the rear.
They marched behind the Philistine leaders.
passages.original: וְסַרְנֵ֤י פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ עֹֽבְרִ֔ים לְמֵא֖וֹת וְלַאֲלָפִ֑ים וְדָוִ֣ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֗יו עֹֽבְרִ֛ים בָּאַחֲרֹנָ֖ה עִם־ אָכִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: Then the commanders of the Philistines asked, “What about these Hebrews?” Achish replied, “Is this not David, the servant of King Saul of Israel? He has been with me all these days, even years, and from the day he defected until today I have found no fault in him.”
passages.sermon:
The commanders of the Philistines spoke.
They asked, “Who are these Hebrews?”
Achish answered the commanders.
He said, “This is David.”
David served Saul.
Saul is the king of Israel.
David has stayed with me.
He has been with me for days.
He has also been with me for years.
From the day David came to me until today, I have found nothing wrong in him.
I have found no fault in David.
passages.original: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ שָׂרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים מָ֖ה הָעִבְרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אָכִ֜ישׁ אֶל־ שָׂרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים הֲלֽוֹא־ זֶ֨ה דָוִ֜ד עֶ֣בֶד׀ שָׁא֣וּל מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה אִתִּי֙ זֶ֤ה יָמִים֙ אוֹ־ זֶ֣ה שָׁנִ֔ים וְלֹֽא־ מָצָ֤אתִי בוֹ֙ מְא֔וּמָה מִיּ֥וֹם נָפְל֖וֹ עַד־ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ

passages.text: But the commanders of the Philistines were angry with Achish and told him, “Send that man back and let him return to the place you assigned him. He must not go down with us into battle only to become our adversary during the war. What better way for him to regain the favor of his master than with the heads of our men?
passages.sermon:
The commanders of the Philistines became angry with Achish.
They spoke to Achish.
They said, “Send this man back.
Let him return to the place where you assigned him.
He must not go down with us into battle.
He might become our enemy during the war.
He could try to win back his master’s favor.
He might do this by attacking our men and bringing their heads.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְצְפ֨וּ עָלָ֜יו שָׂרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ לוֹ֩ שָׂרֵ֨י פְלִשְׁתִּ֜ים הָשֵׁ֣ב אֶת־ הָאִ֗ישׁ וְיָשֹׁב֙ אֶל־ מְקוֹמוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִפְקַדְתּ֣וֹ שָׁ֔ם וְלֹֽא־ יֵרֵ֤ד עִמָּ֙נוּ֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְלֹא־ יִֽהְיֶה־ לָּ֥נוּ לְשָׂטָ֖ן בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וּבַמֶּ֗ה יִתְרַצֶּ֥ה זֶה֙ אֶל־ אֲדֹנָ֔יו הֲל֕וֹא בְּרָאשֵׁ֖י הָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים הָהֵֽם׃

passages.text: Is this not the David about whom they sing in their dances: ‘Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands’?”
passages.sermon:
David was a famous warrior from Israel.
People sang songs about David.
They sang these songs while they danced.
The songs said, “Saul has killed his thousands.”
The songs also said, “David has killed his tens of thousands.”
passages.original: הֲלוֹא־ זֶ֣ה דָוִ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֧ר יַעֲנוּ־ ל֛וֹ בַּמְּחֹל֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר הִכָּ֤ה שָׁאוּל֙ בַּֽאֲלָפָ֔יו וְדָוִ֖ד בְּרִבְבֹתוֹ׃ס

passages.text: So Achish summoned David and told him, “As surely as the LORD lives, you have been upright in my sight, and it seems right that you should march in and out with me in the army, because I have found no fault in you from the day you came to me until this day. But you have no favor in the sight of the leaders.
passages.sermon:
Achish was a Philistine ruler.
Achish called David to him.
Achish spoke to David.
Achish said, “As surely as the LORD lives, you have been upright in my sight.
You have acted rightly before me.
You have gone out and come in with me in the army.
I have found no fault in you.
From the day you came to me until today, you have done nothing wrong.
But the Philistine leaders do not approve of you.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אָכִ֜ישׁ אֶל־ דָּוִ֗ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵ֠לָיו חַי־ יְהוָ֞ה כִּי־ יָשָׁ֣ר אַתָּ֗ה וְט֣וֹב בְּ֠עֵינַי צֵאתְךָ֨ וּבֹאֲךָ֤ אִתִּי֙ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה כִּ֠י לֹֽא־ מָצָ֤אתִֽי בְךָ֙ רָעָ֔ה מִיּ֛וֹם בֹּאֲךָ֥ אֵלַ֖י עַד־ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וּבְעֵינֵ֥י הַסְּרָנִ֖ים לֹֽא־ ט֥וֹב אָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: Therefore turn back now and go in peace, so that you will not do anything to displease the leaders of the Philistines.”
passages.sermon:
Achish was the king of Gath.
Achish spoke to David.
Achish told David to return.
Achish told David to go in peace.
Achish did not want David to upset the Philistine leaders.
Achish wanted David to avoid doing anything wrong in their eyes.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֥ה שׁ֖וּב וְלֵ֣ךְ בְּשָׁל֑וֹם וְלֹֽא־ תַעֲשֶׂ֣ה רָ֔ע בְּעֵינֵ֖י סַרְנֵ֥י פְלִשְׁתִּֽים׃ס

passages.text: “But what have I done?” David replied. “What have you found against your servant, from the day I came to you until today, to keep me from going along to fight against the enemies of my lord the king?”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Achish.
David was a servant of Achish.
David said, “What have I done?”
David asked Achish, “What have you found against your servant?”
David had been with Achish from the first day until that day.
David said, “From the day I came before you until today, what have you found against me?”
David wanted to go and fight against the enemies of Achish, the king.
David asked, “Why can I not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־ אָכִ֗ישׁ כִּ֣י מֶ֤ה עָשִׂ֙יתִי֙ וּמַה־ מָּצָ֣אתָ בְעַבְדְּךָ֔ מִיּוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיִ֣יתִי לְפָנֶ֔יךָ עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֣י לֹ֤א אָבוֹא֙ וְנִלְחַ֔מְתִּי בְּאֹיְבֵ֖י אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Achish replied, “I know that you are as pleasing in my sight as an angel of God. But the commanders of the Philistines have said, ‘He must not go into battle with us.’
passages.sermon:
Achish was the king of Gath, a Philistine city.
Achish spoke to David.
Achish said, "I know you are good in my eyes."
Achish said, "You are as pleasing to me as an angel of God."
But the commanders of the Philistines spoke to Achish.
The commanders said, "David must not go into battle with us."
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַן אָכִישׁ֮ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־ דָּוִד֒ יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּ֣י ט֥וֹב אַתָּ֛ה בְּעֵינַ֖י כְּמַלְאַ֣ךְ אֱלֹהִ֑ים אַ֣ךְ שָׂרֵ֤י פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ אָֽמְר֔וּ לֹֽא־ יַעֲלֶ֥ה עִמָּ֖נוּ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: Now then, get up early in the morning, along with your master’s servants who came with you, and go as soon as it is light.”
passages.sermon:
Achish spoke to David.
Achish was a Philistine king.
Achish told David what to do.
Achish said, “Get up early in the morning.
Take your master’s servants who came with you.
All of you must get up early in the morning.
When it is light, go on your way.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְעַבְדֵ֥י אֲדֹנֶ֖יךָ אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֣אוּ אִתָּ֑ךְ וְהִשְׁכַּמְתֶּ֣ם בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְא֥וֹר לָכֶ֖ם וָלֵֽכוּ׃

passages.text: So David and his men got up early in the morning to return to the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of his men.
David and his men got up early in the morning.
They prepared to leave.
They went back to the land of the Philistines.
The Philistines were a powerful people.
The Philistines went up to Jezreel.
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם דָּוִ֜ד ה֤וּא וַֽאֲנָשָׁיו֙ לָלֶ֣כֶת בַּבֹּ֔קֶר לָשׁ֖וּב אֶל־ אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים עָל֥וּ יִזְרְעֶֽאל׃ס
